title: RAW UNREVIEWED: two kooiin entries describe one harvested organ class or share an entry formula
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The exact first prose group kooiin occurs on the admitted f2v and f29v Herbal pages, whose pictures depict different plants with compact underground structures. GDT1059 found a following TCH family on both pages but also on 29/87 comparison heads, so this neighbour cannot select a rootstock meaning. GDT1062 verifies the published f2v form and position in IT2a but leaves its BORAGO value unbound. An exploratory whole reading could make kooiin a common harvested underground-organ or drug-class subject in both entries; a rival makes it a generic entry opener and assigns each page its own pictured plant as the subject. Preserve every complete paragraph and exact group in all three alternate readings. Only a separately owned organ or subject relation and distinct consequences elsewhere in both complete entries could discriminate them. No botanical species or translated word follows now. Primaries: experiments/yolo/gdt1059_kooiin_header_quality_base_rate/REPORT.md; experiments/yolo/gdt1062_schechter_plant_label_source_alignment/REPORT.md.

design.mechanism: A repeated complete Herbal head selects the same harvested organ or material class across two visibly different plants.
design.unit: The two exact kooiin heads and the complete admitted f2v and f29v prose records with their already admitted images and all three alternative transcriptions.
design.contrast: Shared underground-organ or drug-class subject across both entries versus a generic entry opener followed by page-specific plant subjects; species identity is a third, separately unbound rival.
design.prediction: Under the organ-class reading, one fixed kooiin role must govern both full records, and each record must be able to attach at least one independently grounded organ-specific assertion to the depicted different plants. Under the entry-opener reading, kooiin need not carry that organ reference and the full records may have different subjects. A repeated TCH neighbour, visual root similarity, or a first-position match alone does not distinguish them. If both complete readings remain coherent without an independent subject owner, retain nonselection.
design.prior_blockers: GDT1059 measured a high TCH base rate and left rootstock versus generic head open; GDT1062 leaves published species names unbound; GDT623/GDT768 working glosses cannot provide independent referents.
design.scope: Exploratory reading on already admitted f2v/f29v only; no reserve use, species assignment or score-ready edge claim.
